name: Truck Inspection Checklist
description: A DOT-style pre-trip inspection for commercial trucks covering tires, brakes, lights, coupling, fluids and load securement.

items.text: Check engine oil level and condition
Check coolant level and inspect the radiator
Check power steering and washer fluid
Inspect belts and hoses for cracks or wear
Look for leaks under the engine and components
Check the battery is secure with clean connections
Check tire pressure and inflate to spec
Measure tread depth against the legal minimum
Inspect for cuts, bulges, uneven wear or debris
Check for missing or loose lug nuts and rust streaks
Inspect rims for cracks or damage
Confirm dual tires are not touching and valve caps are present
Perform an air brake leak-down and build-up test
Check the low-air warning and emergency brake function
Inspect brake chambers, slack adjusters and linings
Check brake drums or rotors for cracks or wear
Inspect air lines and connections for leaks or damage
Drain air tanks of moisture as required
Test headlights on low and high beam
Check brake lights, tail lights and turn signals
Confirm clearance, marker and reflector lights work
Test the four-way hazard flashers
Check the horn and backup alarm
Clean lenses and reflectors for visibility
Confirm the fifth wheel is locked with no gap
items.note: Check the locking jaws are closed around the kingpin

items.text: Inspect the kingpin and apron for damage
Check that the release arm is in the locked position
Connect and inspect air lines and the electrical cord
Check landing gear is fully raised and secured
Inspect the trailer frame, doors and mud flaps
Test steering play, mirrors and the windshield
Check seat belt, gauges and warning lights
Confirm the fire extinguisher and emergency triangles are present
Verify the load is secured, balanced and within weight limits
Inspect straps, chains, tarps and tie-downs
Confirm required permits and paperwork are aboard

faq.a: A pre-trip inspection is a systematic walk-around and operational check a commercial driver performs before driving, covering tires, brakes, lights, coupling, fluids and the load. It confirms the truck is safe and roadworthy and is required by regulations in many jurisdictions.

faq.q: How long does a truck inspection take?
faq.a: A thorough pre-trip inspection typically takes around fifteen minutes once it is routine, longer when defects are found. Rushing it defeats the purpose; the goal is to find problems in the yard rather than discover them on the road.

faq.q: What should I check on the coupling system?
faq.a: Confirm the fifth wheel is locked with no gap, the kingpin is seated, the locking jaws are closed, the release arm is in position, and air and electrical lines are connected and free of leaks or damage. A bad coupling can cause a trailer to separate.

faq.q: What if I find a defect during inspection?
faq.a: Document the defect, report it per your company's procedures and do not operate the truck if the defect makes it unsafe or out of compliance. Have repairs done by a qualified technician and keep records as required by the regulations that apply to you.

faq.q: Can I print this truck inspection checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it in the cab and work through tires, brakes, lights, coupling, fluids and load checks before every trip.
